Idea: a contract assurance mode tuned for AI agent callers. Generate property-based test traffic from the OpenAPI schema and run it against the mock, checking that responses stay inside the contract across odd ranges, boundary values, and repeated failing calls, the patterns agent callers actually produce. Then treat detected contract drift as a release blocker, not a warning.

Why it matters: MockForge already has contract validation and drift detection. The gap this fills is assurance from the caller's side: agents probe ranges humans never try, retry failures aggressively, and build plans on mock behavior. If the mock drifts from the schema, agent-built integrations fail downstream in ways that are hard to trace back.

## Description

Some test doubles for internal collaborators copy the real class's behaviour by hand: a `side_effect`, or a stub return value that stands in for real logic. When the real contract changes, nothing makes the fake change with it, and the tests keep passing against behaviour the code no longer has.

**What bit us:** in #4148 (spec 154), `AppRegistry.set_status` started returning `None` for writes that change nothing, including a first registration. The lifecycle tests' `mock_registry` still used `fake_set_status` (`tests/unit/core/_fixtures_app_lifecycle.py`), which returns a `StatusChange` for every write, and `get_status` returned `NOT_STARTED` no matter what. Because of that, `test_emits_not_started_event` kept asserting a NOT_STARTED event on a first start that the real code never sends. CodeRabbit caught it in review, and nothing in the suite did. #4148 fixed that fake: `get_status` now follows the writes, and the tests that assert on emitted events now use `real_registry_service`. That fixes one fake. The pattern is still everywhere.

## Scope

Audit the hand-written fakes of **internal** collaborators, the ones that re-implement logic instead of standing in at a system boundary, for drift from the class they replace. Starting points:

- `tests/unit/core/_fixtures_app_lifecycle.py`: `mock_registry` (`fake_set_status`, `set_registry_apps`, `last_written_status`, and the stubbed `refusal_reason`, `get_needs_restart` and `is_debug_captured`)
- `tests/unit/app_factory/conftest.py`: `mock_registry` (independent `get` / `get_live_apps` stubs)
- `tests/support/mock_hassette.py` (`make_mock_hassette`), `tests/support/web_mocks.py` (`create_hassette_stub`), `tests/support/state_proxy_mocks.py`, `tests/support/websocket_mocks.py`
- any other `side_effect=` in `tests/unit/**/conftest.py` / `_fixtures_*.py` that encodes a rule from `src/`

For each fake, decide on one of:
1. **Replace it with the real class.** For example, `AppRegistry` is cheap to build, and `seed_running` / `seed_failed` put it in any state.
2. **Wrap the real class** (`Mock(wraps=real)`) when the test needs call recording.
3. **Keep it and pin it with a contract test** that runs the same inputs through the fake and the real class and asserts they give the same results, so changing the contract fails a test.

#1356 covers contract checks for `make_mock_hassette` in particular. Fold its findings in, or link them, rather than duplicating them.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] An inventory of the internal-collaborator fakes under `tests/` that re-implement `src/` logic, each with the decision above.
- [ ] Every fake marked "replace" or "wrap" is migrated, and the tests that were asserting behaviour the real class doesn't have are fixed and listed in the PR.
- [ ] Every fake that's kept has a contract test that fails when it drifts from the real class.
- [ ] `tests/TESTING.md` says when a hand-written fake of an internal class is acceptable and that it needs a contract test.
title: Audit test fakes of internal collaborators for drift from the real contract

Every Vitest page test and every Playwright spec runs against `web/src/mocks/handlers.ts`, 6013 hand-written lines that reimplement the API. On top of merged C0 [PR #8](https://github.com/Pickle-Pee/smm_ai_helper_web/pull/8), prepare Next.js frontend for FastAPI Web API v2 while **keeping production/default behavior strictly mock-only**, without any real API/AI requests, auth claims, backend changes, DNS/Caddy/Docker changes, or deployment changes.

Typed **WebApiV2Client** with same-origin `/api/v2`, injected `fetch`, `credentials: same-origin`, JSON decoding and typed discriminated errors; CSRF on unsafe methods once session exists, no browser bot token or Telegram identity headers; abort/timeout, explicit 401/403/404/409/429/503, HTML/empty 502/504 support. - No fake AI success, no fake remote persistence, no touching production services.

## Question

How will fixtures stay aligned with real app/result contracts, and which behavior must be verified by frontend scenario tests, pure Domain tests, real business/PostgreSQL integration tests and fully integrated E2E journeys so simulated success cannot hide broken integration?

This is a HITL verification/fixture-ownership decision, using the agreed scenario matrix and chosen seam. Honor the developer's selected structured setup under fixtures/ or mocks/: use editable `*.mock.json` response payloads for desired successful/error outcomes, aligned to the real response contracts. Do not require a TypeScript scenario engine, response sequencer or mutable dataset. Treat latency/transport controls as optional future scope unless explicitly selected. The developer requires one consumption path and one mock mechanism, with a simple setup for changing and extending data; see [the clarification](https://github.com/3mrhussein/findeg/issues/531#issuecomment-6425104616). Reuse scenario definitions across development and deliberately configured frontend tests, without parallel browser/server/action fixtures or UI mock conditionals. Avoid unnecessary directory/configuration layers; define the minimum extension steps for an existing response and a new endpoint scenario. Directory ownership and reuse across apps remain part of this question. See [the developer direction](https://github.com/3mrhussein/findeg/issues/531#issuecomment-6423605343) and [current official Next.js testing findings](https://github.com/3mrhussein/findeg/issues/531#issuecomment-6423636961). Preserve existing Vitest/Cypress tooling unless evidence warrants a separately agreed change. Define who owns each fixture/result shape, which Domain values and input/result types are derived, how fixtures/scenarios change alongside real contracts, and what checks detect drift in fields, error variants and observable outcomes without mirroring the implementation.

Distinguish compile-time shape checks from behavior verification. Mocked scenarios must not implement a parallel set of business rules. Real PostgreSQL integration coverage must continue to exercise context-owned operations, authorization, Quote/reconfirmation, Order Acceptance, transaction/locking and stock effects, idempotency and Outbox behavior; pure Domain tests keep rule coverage. Inspect existing suites before adding or relocating checks.

Define critical integrated E2E journeys through both real apps sharing PostgreSQL, including the app-to-business integration seams omitted by frontend mocks. State how those suites select the integrated path, reset/isolate data and handle local delivery without silently invoking the mock mode. Keep real external delivery credentials unnecessary for everyday mock work. Use the existing PostgreSQL test lifecycle under `configs/vitest/postgres/global-setup.ts` as an inspection lead.

Produce a scenario-to-test-lane responsibility matrix, fixture ownership/drift policy, and a precise list of retained, added or currently missing checks. Classify existing baseline gaps honestly. Do not invent passing evidence or defer every integration concern to E2E. Resolve only through live human agreement on coverage and maintenance cost.

Consult wayfinder, grilling, domain-modeling and codebase-design. Any new missing external fact or selected prototype graduates as its own ticket.

## Context

Tier A runs each connector's action handlers against the in-process emulator, with no Kibana. Part of it already exists:

- **Requests are covered by the contract test (#295686).** At PR time it re-records every connector with artifacts against its committed snapshot: real axios on the emulator's `fetch`, with the connector's own auth type, and generated inputs in four variants per action (`required`, `all`, `boundary` at the schema's upper bounds, and every `enum` value). Any request the emulator rejects fails the test. That covers the original "harness with boundary inputs, green for all connectors against their snapshot mock".
- **The run against the latest vendor spec moves to the drift workflow (#295692)**, which owns the two-mock result (snapshot mock passes, latest-spec mock fails: vendor drift broke the connector).

What nothing checks yet is the other direction: how handlers **handle the responses** the spec allows. The recorder answers every request with one sampled success response, so a handler that loops forever on pagination, silently drops the last page, or crashes on an error status the spec declares passes every current check. For agent tools these break a call whatever the request looked like.

Depends on: #295684, #295685, #295686

## Scope

Add response-side modes to the contract test, reusing its harness (`createContractContext` / `runAction`) and generated inputs, rather than a separate runner:

- **Boundary responses**: run each action with `sampling: 'boundary'` (values at the schema's bounds: longest strings, largest numbers, fullest arrays, last enum values), and fail when a handler throws or corrupts values.
- **Pagination**: for every operation with a `pagination` descriptor in the manifest, run the paginating actions against collections of 0 items, fewer than one page, exactly one page and several pages (`collectionSize`), and assert that they stop within a bounded number of requests and return every item (or stop where their own limit says).
- **Error responses**: for each operation an action calls, serve each error status the spec declares (and 429 / 5xx where the spec has none), and assert that the handler fails with an explanatory error instead of crashing or returning a success-shaped result.
- Report failures per connector and action, with the response that caused them, so the drift workflow (#295692) can include them in its issues.
- Opt-outs per action in `fixtures.json` with a reason, for handlers whose behavior is intentionally different (e.g. an action that deliberately returns one page).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The contract test runs the boundary-response, pagination and error-response modes for all connectors with artifacts, and they pass or have documented opt-outs.
- [ ] A deliberately broken handler fixture fails each mode: one that loops on pagination, one that drops the last page, and one that crashes on a declared error status.
- [ ] Results can be included in the drift workflow's per-connector issue (#295692).

## Goal
Author the canonical example responses that both sides build against. The frontend's mock mode serves them; the backend's conformance tests (#10 (B15)) validate every file against its Pydantic schemas. Any drift between the two implementations therefore shows up on day 1 instead of at integration.

This is the one time Adit's side writes in `contract/`. It ships as a single PR from a `contract/fixtures` branch that Jayden reviews (target: merged by T+3). After it merges, fixtures change only through the contract-change process in [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/jayden-crypto/ghostwatch/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).

## Scope
- One JSON file per endpoint response in `contract/fixtures/`, named `<resource>.<operation>[.<variant>].json`, for example `agents.list.json`, `executions.trace.exe_<id>.json`, `investigations.get.confirmed.json`, `error.side_effect_authorization_required.json`

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The fixtures tell one coherent story matching the demo in [plan §5 SDK and demo](https://github.com/jayden-crypto/ghostwatch/blob/main/PROJECT_PLAN.md#5-sdk-and-demo-backend-side-b10b11b13): three agents (`research-assistant`, `invoice-processor`, `support-triage`); a healthy research run; the schema-change failure (`KeyError: 'results'`) with its **confirmed** investigation citing signature `missing_key_in_upstream_output`; the ghost-completion invoice run with a **critical** anomaly; `excessive_retries` and `duration_spike` on support-triage; one completed sandbox replay with outcome `fixed`
- [ ] The same ids are used across all files, so every link resolves in mock mode (execution → trace → anomaly → investigation → replay)
- [ ] Ids are `prefix_` + 32 lowercase hex; timestamps are UTC with milliseconds and a `Z` suffix ([contract §0 Global conventions](https://github.com/jayden-crypto/ghostwatch/blob/main/contract/API_CONTRACT.md#0-global-conventions))
- [ ] Every key the contract lists is present; absent values are `null`, never omitted
- [ ] Every value of every enum in [contract §1 Enums](https://github.com/jayden-crypto/ghostwatch/blob/main/contract/API_CONTRACT.md#1-enums-exact-string-values) appears at least once somewhere, so every badge gets exercised
